newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair dismisses Charles and Camilla reports.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair dismisses Charles and Camilla reports.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair's office on Monday dismissed reports that the government was ready to give its approval for royal heir Prince Charles to marry his lover Camilla Parker Bowles.
The mass-selling Sun newspaper said Blair was ready to give the couple the go-ahead as long as they could win the support of the British people and the Church of England.
But a close aide said the prime minister had expressed no views on the matter and was irritated by the reports. "These stories are completely and totally untrue," he said.
"The prime minister has never expressed any view privately or publicly and those that say he has and newspapers that say he has are not telling the truth," he added.
"He is in a position where in his judgement it is not wise to express views that can be so easily misrepresented."

Charles has been taking steps to give Camilla greater public exposure as the woman in his life. She hit the headlines earlier this month when Charles hosted a glittering 50th birthday party for her at his country residence, Highgrove.
But many Britons blame her for the break-up of Charles's 15-year marriage to Princess Diana and say they could never accept Camilla, who is also divorced, as queen of England.
As prime minister, Blair has sweeping powers to advise Queen Elizabeth over the succession to the throne.
He has made clear he has no sympathy with some Labour Party members who want to do away with the monarchy.
The aide also dismissed reports that one of Blair's closest colleagues, Minister without Portfolio Peter Mandelson, had held talks with Charles, 48, Camilla, 50, and Diana, 36.
He said media reports had "misrepresented" a party where the guests had included both Mandelson and Camilla.
